title: Planning a Small Farm Business
summary: This lesson teaches how to create a simple budget, research your market, and keep basic records for a small farm. With these tools you can make informed decisions and track your farm’s progress.

sections.heading: Creating a Simple Budget
sections.body:
Start by listing all expected costs for the first year: seeds, fertilizer, water, tools, and any labor you will pay. Next, estimate your expected income from the crops you plan to sell. Subtract the total costs from the total income to see if you will have a profit or a shortfall.

If the numbers show a shortfall, look for ways to reduce costs (e.g., buying seeds in bulk) or increase income (e.g., adding a higher‑value crop). Keep the budget on paper or in a spreadsheet so you can update it each month.

sections.heading: Doing Basic Market Research
sections.body:
Talk to local buyers such as grocery stores, restaurants, and farmers’ market vendors to learn what products they need and how much they will pay. Visit nearby farms to see what they sell and at what price. Write down the information in a simple table: product, price per unit, and demand level.

Use this table to choose crops that match local demand and give you a good price. Remember that a crop that sells well locally may be more profitable than a high‑yield crop that no one wants to buy.

sections.heading: Simple Record‑Keeping
sections.body:
Record every expense and every sale in a notebook or spreadsheet. Include the date, description, amount spent or earned, and the product involved. At the end of each month, add up totals for each category and compare them to your budget.

Also keep a log of farm activities: planting dates, fertilizer applications, pest observations, and harvest dates. This information helps you spot patterns, such as which crops need more water or which pests appear at certain times.

key_terms.meaning: A plan that estimates all expected costs and revenues for a set period.
The process of gathering information about buyers, prices, and demand for products.
The total money earned from selling farm products.
Any cost incurred to run the farm, such as seeds, water, or labor.
Systematically writing down financial and farm activity data for future reference.

quiz.q: What is the first step in creating a farm budget?
quiz.why: You must know all costs before you can compare them to income.

quiz.q: Why is market research important for a small farm?
options: It tells you how much fertilizer to use
It helps you choose crops that buyers want
It reduces the need for irrigation
quiz.why: Understanding buyer demand guides crop selection and pricing.

quiz.q: Which of the following should be recorded in a farm activity log?
quiz.why: Planting dates are essential for tracking crop growth and yields.

quiz.q: If your monthly expenses exceed your revenue, you should:
quiz.why: Adjusting prices or reducing costs helps bring the budget back into balance.

flashcards.back: A plan that lists expected costs and expected income for a period.
Money earned from selling farm products.
Any cost incurred to run the farm, such as seeds, water, or labor.
Gathering information about buyers, prices, and demand for your products.
Writing down financial transactions and farm activities to track performance.
